A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Watermark Anything Model work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support a reliable comparison. V2 retains the original scientific material and adds Appendix G.

before.justification: V1 reports original watermarking experiments on COCO, DIV2k, and generated images, including detection, decoding, localization, and multiple-message results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, neural-attack evaluations, a watermark-strength sweep, and overlapping-watermark detection results.

M1.justification: The embedder, extractor, losses, two-stage training, JND attenuation, and DBSCAN decoding remain unchanged. Appendix G.4 tests the existing watermark-strength parameter; G.1's larger-payload training alternatives are suggestions, not implemented method changes.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds global neural-purification and reconstruction attacks using DiffPure and VAE, plus fully overlapping watermarks carrying different messages. These substantially extend input conditions beyond the original editing, splicing, and disjoint multiple-watermark scenarios. Existing dataset coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds MBRS and CIN to the COCO comparisons; both also participate in Table 9's new attack evaluation. Prior comparators remain. FIN is newly discussed and cited but has no reported comparison results.

E3.justification: Existing training and evaluation protocols remain unchanged. Supplementary protocols add MBRS message repetition and soft voting, CIN's 30-bit decoding without detection, attack comparisons indexed by reconstruction PSNR, an alpha_JND sweep under combined transformations, and a one-versus-two overlapping-watermark control on 100 COCO images.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained training-stage ablation and DBSCAN sensitivity analysis, G.3-G.5 add substantial analyses of neural-removal robustness, the visibility-versus-robustness effect of watermark strength, and detection under complete watermark overlap. These examine previously untested failure conditions and parameter trade-offs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars for these evaluations. The new tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained result tables and plots are unchanged, while Tables 8-11 add substantial results. WAM reaches 49.1% bit accuracy under DiffPure at 24.9 dB and 53.7% under VAE attack at 25.5 dB. The strength sweep trades 44.1 dB/71.0% accuracy for 34.8 dB/91.9%. One and two overlapping watermarks both yield 100/100 detections. These are added evaluations, not improvements on unchanged v1 results.

T1.justification: The detection and decoding definitions, training equations, DBSCAN description, and JND mathematics remain unchanged, including Equations 1-11. Appendix G adds empirical discussion without new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list, and substantive conclusion retain the same claims about segmentation-based watermarking, two-stage training, competitive robustness, localization, and multiple-message extraction. The conclusion's added notice directs readers to supplementary experiments without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix G further explains the chosen capacity-versus-robustness operating point, acknowledges neural purification as a limitation outside the main focus, and interprets severe VAE results relative to MBRS and TrustMark. It also explains inference-time strength adjustment and the benefit of separating detection from decoding under overlap.

D1.justification: G.2 documents MBRS repetition/averaging, CIN payload handling, and distortion scaling for comparable PSNR. G.4 explains adjusting alpha_JND at inference without retraining. Existing architecture, hardware, training, and code/model access disclosures are retained; the abstract's reformatted repository reference does not establish new availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds the FIN reference by Fang et al. (2023). G.2 expands positioning against MBRS and CIN, already cited in v1, by discussing their operating points relative to WAM's emphasis on small watermarked areas. The original related-work sections otherwise retain their substance.

P1.justification: Sections 1-6 and Appendices A-F remain largely verbatim and in the same order. V2 adds Appendix G with five subsections, a conclusion signpost, and limited wording and author-affiliation edits.

P2.justification: The document switches from the branded report layout to ICLR formatting, replacing the shaded title/abstract panel and changing typography, headings, headers, and float placement throughout. Tables 8-11 are added, and retained figures and tables are resized or relocated, including Figures 10 and 11 sharing a page. Existing figure content is preserved.

improvement.justification: Appendix G strengthens empirical support through additional comparators and clarifies applicability through neural-attack failures and a measured visibility-versus-robustness trade-off. These are useful extensions to v1's already extensive evaluation. Their reach remains bounded: attack reproduction details are limited, and the overlap experiment establishes detection on 100 images rather than recovery of both messages. The original payload and perceptual-quality limitations remain.
